newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 17.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - July 17.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY

- Forum held by People's Daily and Seeking Truth magazine to study speech by President Jiang Zemin's recent speech urges people to hold high banner of Deng Xiaoping's theory of building socialism with Chinese characteristics.
- Vietnamese Communist Party General Secretary Do Muoi leaves for Kunming.
- Delegation led by Vice-Premier Zou Jiahua to go to Hohhot to attend celebrations for 50th anniversary of founding of Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.
- Output of summer grain in Xinjiang at 4.47 million tonnes
- Total output of early rice in Hubei province at 4.175 million tonnes
- State purchases 16.04 million tonnes of wheat by July 5
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- State Council issues circular banning illegal buying and selling of renminbi

- Politburo Standing Committee member Hu Jintao meets delegation from Japan's Liberal Democratic Party, headed by secretary-general Kato Koichi, and says Chinese Communist Party willing to increase exchanges and cooperation with LDP.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- Output of building material firms reached 35.86 billion yuan in first five months, up 5.44 percent from a year ago
- Industrial and Commercial Bank of China completes sales of 88 percent of state bonds in first half
CHINA SECURITIES
- Bank of China to provide 3.8 billion yuan loans to Konka Group
- Sales of colour televisions expected to exceed 20 million in 1997, up 20 percent from last year
ECONOMIC INFORMATION DAILY
- By end-June, People's Insurance Company of China Property insurance premiums up 14 percent from year-ago period
CHINA DAILY
- Taiwan hands over two suspected hijackers to Red Cross Society of China. The two will be charged.
- Worsening drought in the north and a possible devastating flood in the south prompt Vice-Premier Jiang Chunyun to call on local authorities to fight for this autumn's harvest.
- Chinese courts nationwide handle 5,296 intellectual property rights disputes in past 17 months and concluded 4,735 cases in same period, senior judge says
